headline: A 2018 law lets the VA help disabled veterans in its job-training program pay for home modifications, up to a set dollar limit.
what_it_does: The law allows the Department of Veterans Affairs to help veterans with service-connected disabilities who are in its vocational rehabilitation and employment program pay for changes to their homes that they need. Help cannot be given if it would duplicate other benefits. The total help a veteran can receive is capped at $77,307, though the VA can waive that cap when needed for the veteran's rehabilitation program, and the limit is to be raised over time. The law also says the VA does not have to provide mortgage life insurance to veterans under age 70 who receive this home-adaptation help.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans with service-connected disabilities enrolled in VA vocational rehabilitation and employment
who_it_affects.how: They may get VA help paying for home changes they need, up to the stated cap unless the VA grants a waiver.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans under age 70 who receive home-adaptation help
who_it_affects.how: The VA is not required to give them mortgage life insurance as part of this assistance.
The VA must report to Congress every two years, starting October 1, 2019, on how it uses its waiver authority.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on June 1, 2018. The biennial reporting requirement begins October 1, 2019, and the summary does not give a separate start date for the home-adaptation assistance.
